summary: Tested the new /api/market/* CoinGecko backend proxy + CoinDetail scrollspy + ETH/SOL/LTC coin pages + Markets page + UserDashboard rates. All 6 backend proxy tests pass. Frontend features largely work: BTC/ETH/SOL/LTC render with correct titles, sections, whitepaper, and live EUR prices once backend cache is warm. Markets page shows 0 occurrences of '0,00'. Mobile scrollspy works correctly (TOC order=-1 above article, active section transitions #what -> #governance -> #cycle). Found 2 notable issues: desktop scrollspy can stick on an earlier section because .find() picks the first visible id in document order; and CoinChart header shows '0,00 €' instead of a dash fallback while market data is still loading / failing.

minor.issue: Frequently 503 due to CoinGecko free-tier rate limits. Cache only helps once one request succeeds. ETH & SOL chart polylines were missing in UI until a request lands.

ui_bugs.issue: When market data has not loaded yet, header renders eur(undefined) -> '0,00 €'. Should fall back to '—' like the Market Data grid. Spec explicitly says prices must never render as 0,00 EUR.

ids.find(id => visible.has(id)) always picks the first-in-doc-order visible section, so active TOC entry gets 'stuck' on an earlier heading on desktop (observed #holders remained active at scroll y=2000, 4000, 7000 on /markets/bitcoin). Should pick the LAST visible section (reading position) or the closest to top. Mobile is unaffected because viewport is small.

action_items: In CoinChart: render '—' (or hide the price node) when current is null/undefined instead of eur(0).

Fix scrollspy selection in CoinDetail.tsx: replace ids.find(... visible.has) with picking the LAST visible id (e.g. ids.filter(i=>visible.has(i)).pop()) OR compute active via smallest positive top offset relative to a header line.
Optional: add a user-friendly placeholder when /api/market/chart/{coin} is 503 (small 'Chart temporarily unavailable, retrying…' hint).
critical_code_review_comments: market_data._cached locks dict grows unbounded (locks never evicted) - low risk but worth noting.

CoinDetail.tsx getJSON fallback resolves to [] on failure, then setMarket(j && j.id ? j : null). Good - but CoinChart does not check for null before computing eur(). This is the root cause of the 0,00 bug.
scrollspy uses ids.find() with doc-order precedence; UX convention is to highlight the LAST section whose top crossed the header, not the first intersecting.
test_credentials: testuser1@example.com / Test1234 (login OK, dashboard loaded with no 0,00)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend proxy is solid - all 4 endpoints (coins, coin/{id}, chart/{id}, simple-price) return correct JSON. Primary remaining work is 2 frontend bugs listed above. CoinGecko rate-limits the preview egress IP aggressively; warm cache for ~60s before judging prices.
rca of the issue: 0,00 price RCA: CoinDetail's useEffect sets market=null when market fetch fails or until it resolves. CoinChart renders eur(current?.current_price). The eur() helper does `v || 0` so undefined becomes 0 and formatter outputs '0,00 €'. Fix: guard the JSX with `{current ? eur(current.current_price) : '—'}`. Scrollspy RCA: IntersectionObserver callback stores all currently intersecting ids in a Set, then `ids.find(id => visible.has(id))` returns the first in document order. When two sections are simultaneously intersecting (common on tall desktop viewports) the earlier one wins forever. Fix: `const last=[...ids].reverse().find(i=>visible.has(i))` OR track entries and pick the one with greatest boundingClientRect.top <= header offset.
